description: 2026-09-30 re-baseline: group C supersedes the live inline block that hides the legacy desktop bottom timeline bar in Mobile mode (see docs/baseline-drift.md section 4)

patches.find:
<script>
    // Hides the legacy desktop-style bottom timeline bar when the app's own "Mobile" mode
    // is active. Confirmed live: that bar (day/time readout, July 1/2/3 pills, speed
    // buttons, the credit line) keeps rendering in mobile mode alongside the app's own
    // mobile-native "Tools" bottom sheet -- not something this file ever injects, it's the
    // real app's own React output, just never hidden for this mode. The overlap isn't only
    // cosmetic: confirmed live that with both sets of playback controls present, tapping in
    // that area can land on the legacy bar's own play/next-tick buttons instead of the
    // mobile ones, and they don't keep the same state in sync with each other -- one
    // click landed on a legacy control that jumped the displayed clock forward with the
    // tick counter and unit count left behind, completely out of sync with the display.
    //
    // No access to the app's internals needed: mobile mode is detected the same reliable
    // way used elsewhere in this file -- a real, accessible-name button unique to that
    // mode ("Tools") -- and the legacy bar is found by the one piece of text guaranteed to
    // be in it (the site's own credit line), climbing from there to its positioned
    // ancestor. Checked on a light recurring interval, not a DOM-wide observer, since
    // mobile/desktop mode can be switched at any time from the app's own settings menu.
    (function () {
      var legacyBar = null;

      function findLegacyBar() {
        if (legacyBar && document.body.contains(legacyBar)) return legacyBar;
        // Anchored on the mailto link rather than requiring a single leaf element with the
        // full "Created by: Mike Legere" text -- caught live, that text is actually split
        // across sibling nodes, so no single leaf element's own textContent ever matched.
        // The mailto link is real, single, and unique regardless of how the surrounding
        // text is split.
        var creditEl = document.querySelector('a[href^="mailto:gettysburginteractivemap"]');
        if (!creditEl) return null;
        var node = creditEl;
        for (var i = 0; i < 8 && node; i++, node = node.parentElement) {
          var pos = getComputedStyle(node).position;
          if (pos === 'fixed' || pos === 'absolute') { legacyBar = node; return node; }
        }
        return null;
      }

      function isMobileMode() {
        return !!Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('button')).find(function (b) {
          var text = (b.textContent || '').trim();
          var name = (b.title || b.getAttribute('aria-label') || '').trim();
          return /Tools$/.test(text) || /^Tools$/.test(name);
        });
      }

      function sync() {
        var bar = findLegacyBar();
        if (!bar) return;
        bar.style.display = isMobileMode() ? 'none' : '';
      }

      setInterval(sync, 800);
    })();
  </script>
patches.note: Live (deploy 6abd6d62, not in legacy/dist) added an inline <script> that, every 800 ms, hides the legacy desktop bottom timeline bar when a button ending in 'Tools' exists (Mobile mode), finding the bar through the credit mailto link. Group C never mounts the desktop overlays in the mobile layout (HF-1a), so there is no bar and no credit link to find (measured: rangeInputs 0, credit links 0 in R1b/R1c mobile); on desktop the block only force-resets the bar's inline display every 800 ms. Kept in R0/R1a (no group C: the legacy bar IS mounted in Mobile mode there), removed from R1b on.
